It differs from standard volumetric rendering by operating in screen space on a pre-computed scene texture, using a cone SDF to create directional light shafts that taper from the light source rather than using box or sphere primitives [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly supports all components of the claim: 1) It is a post-processing technique (operating in screen space) using a 'sceneTexture' binding. 2) It uses a 'cone SDF' (function `sdCone`) to define the volume shape. 3) The raymarching originates from the camera/light direction to create light shafts. 4) The geometry is defined by the cone SDF, not box or sphere primitives.

Volumetric Light Shafts (Cone Raymarching) is a post-processing technique that renders volumetric light shafts by raymarching through a cone-shaped volume originating from a light source, using Signed Distance Fields (SDFs) to define the volume shape and noise for density variation [S1, unofficial].

The claim states that Volumetric Light Shafts (Cone Raymarching) is a post-processing technique that renders volumetric light shafts by raymarching through a cone-shaped volume originating from a light source, using Signed Distance Fields (SDFs) to define the volume shape and noise for density variation. Source [S1] provides code for a post-process shader that implements exactly this: it defines a cone using an `sdCone` function (SDF), uses `fbm3D` (noise) to modify the density/shape factor, and performs raymarching through this volume to accumulate light. All specific details in the claim are present in the evidence.
